summary: Japan supports renewables through feed-in tariffs moving to feed-in premiums, runs offshore wind auctions, and has an active corporate PPA market. A 2025 change puts FIT projects first in line for curtailment, raising risk for older projects.

access.reason: Projects are certified for feed-in tariffs or premiums, and offshore wind sites have been auctioned under the 2018 Marine Renewable Energy Act.

terms.reason: The premium scheme links revenue to market prices, and curtailment risk has risen for tariff projects.

ownership.reason: Foreign exchange rules have little impact on normal business, and no foreign ownership cap on generation was found.

build.reason: Curtailment orders apply, and geothermal sites in national parks need several permits and local agreement.

stability.reason: The 2025 curtailment change shifts risk onto existing tariff projects to favour premium projects.

direction.reason: The government keeps moving projects from tariffs to premiums.

access.reason: On-site and off-site corporate PPAs are widely used, physical PPAs through a registered retailer and virtual PPAs directly.

ownership.reason: Foreign exchange rules have little impact on normal business.

stability.reason: Premium projects get priority under the revised curtailment rules, which supports corporate PPAs.

direction.reason: Corporate PPAs under the premium scheme have become increasingly popular.
